_about: What every user-visible claim on the landing page actually is, plus the evidence. STATUS ANSWERS ONE QUESTION: what happens if a visitor goes and tries it right now? THE PLATFORM IS UNDER DEVELOPMENT. Claims describe intent and design and are ASPIRATIONAL BY DESIGN — this is a project site describing where the thing is going, not a sales pitch, and present-tense description of intent is the normal convention for software being built. Do NOT weaken an aspirational claim to satisfy this file; publish its stage instead. THE ONE EXCEPTION: a `live-state` claim asserts a fact about CURRENT conditions rather than about capability. Aspiration cannot cover it, because it is not aspirational — it is a status report, and it is the only kind of claim here that can be false while everyone is being honest.

claims.claim: Pay in with a card and it lands in your group's treasury as USDC on Base, without the platform ever holding it
claims.evidence: Sandbox VERIFIED and WIRED 2026-09-13, 19/19 end-to-end through TWO processes. The provider lives in its own app (apps/peer_xyz_payments, :3010, internal only) behind a vendor-neutral contract; coop-api holds the policy and the contract only — no SDK, no vendor term in its payment module, verified. payment_intent uses the COOP's status vocabulary with provider_payload as the sole vendor home, so a swap is a new app + a config line. The rail declares directToDestination (checked by the seam) and honestly reports canObserve:false (the SDK has no order lookup, so settlement cannot be polled). Attribution stays off-chain and is not group-readable; confirmation emits an event the Temporal lane turns into a receipt keyed peer:<provider_ref>. Settlement is now AUTOMATIC via webhook (14/14): the rail app receives the provider's event at pay.<domain>/webhooks/peer (the only routed path; the control plane 404s), authenticates it with a custom-header derived secret, translates it behind the seam so coop-api never sees a provider payload, dedupes retries on (rail,event_id), and handles CHARGEBACKS/REFUNDS as reversals — the intent goes to `reversed` and the ledger gets a `correction` entry referencing the original receipt, which is never deleted. NOT done: no route exercised with a real JWT; live refused in code; the destination is still the sandbox merchant wallet; the webhook is not yet REGISTERED with the provider (a dashboard action).
claims.fix: Live needs: the shared destination to become the batch router / pool contract (not a wallet), an IP allowlist on the merchant key (empty today), and either a provider webhook or an operator confirmation surface for settlement.
claims.note: sandbox-wired; the rails' visibility (Peer + the P2P counterparty) is the open design question.

vocabulary.works: You can use it today. `note` carries any caveat (e.g. it doesn't persist yet).
vocabulary.in-progress: Partly usable, or actively being built right now.
vocabulary.designed: Settled design, implementation not started. Aspirational — publish the stage, keep the claim.
vocabulary.live-state: Asserts a current fact about running systems. Must be wired to a real source, or removed.
